Brett feels the clean up work should be done by the end of today.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 5/11/2023 to STONEHAVEN ENERGY MGT CO LLC in Howe Twp, Forest county. 78.64(a) - CONTAINMENT AROUND OIL TANKS - For a tank capacity of at least 660 gallons or tanks with a combined capacity of at least 1,320 gallons, the owner or operator failed to construct and maintain a dike or other method of secondary containment which satisfies requirements under 40 CFR 112.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: STONEHAVEN ENERGY MGT CO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 5/11/2023
Violation Code: 78.64(a) - CONTAINMENT AROUND OIL TANKS - For a tank capacity of at least 660 gallons or tanks with a combined capacity of at least 1,320 gallons, the owner or operator failed to construct and maintain a dike or other method of secondary containment which satisfies requirements under 40 CFR 112.
Violation ID: 995092
Permit API: 053-29816
Unconventional: No
County: Forest
Municipality: Howe Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 5/11/2023
Comments: This conventional well is equipped with a pump jack that appears to have been recently produced. A sticker is posted on the pump jack displaying the operator's information, the well's API number is written on the jack. There was no activity onsite during this inspection. An approximate 2' x 5' area of vegetation and soil are stained with a coating of crude oil on the well site from the apparent repeated venting of this well into the atmosphere. The same practice is prevalent at a majority of the well sites on the Warrant 2980 lease and will be addressed in a separate inspection report. A tank battery that is located approximately 250' southeast of well consists of four steel and six plastic storage tanks inside of an earthen diking. There are several areas of stained gravel near the tanks (and at a compressor that is also located inside of the diking) which is indicative of production fluid releases onto the gravel inside of the containment.The exterior (southern) wall of the diking is void of vegetation and the specific conductance (SPC) is elevated (3800 uS/cm per field meter). It appears that the production fluid that has been released into the gravel inside of the tank battery diking has migrated through the southern wall of the containment and into a roadside ditch that flows south towards a cross culvert approximately 200 feet south of the well. Stressed vegetation, elevated SPC readings and abundant deer tracks are present in the ditch between the tank battery and the cross culvert and continue in a channel down to the next lease road (near 053-29533) approximately 300 feet beyond the culvert outlet.Multiple sections of the Warrant 2980 lease roads beyond this well to the vicinity of well #'s 053-29907, 053-29935 and 053-29916 have not been sufficiently maintained. BMPs (ditches and cross culverts) that are installed along these roads are not functioning properly, as a result, accelerated erosion is occurring over various stretches of the road surface. Additional E and S concerns on this lease are documented in the 5/11/23 inspection report for 053-29536 (Warrant 2980 #37).It is requested that documentation of production water disposal from this lease be provided to the Department. Please see the attached Notice of Violation regarding requested information pertaining to the cause of the release and intentions to remediate the contaminated material within and outside of the tank battery.

Report Details
Inspection Client: RICE DRILLING B LLC

Violation Code: 91.34(A) - ACTIVITIES UTILIZING POLLUTANTS - Failure to take necessary measures to prevent the substances from directly or indirectly reaching waters of this Commonwealth, through accident, carelessness, maliciousness, hazards of weather or from another cause.
Violation ID: 8153117
Permit API: 125-27720
Unconventional: Yes
County: Washington
Municipality: North Bethlehem Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 7/18/2023
Comments: On 07/18/2023, an incident inspection was conducted at the Ironman Well Site in response to an incident report received by the Department and submitted by EQT on 07/17/2023 (CTS: 373620). I was accompanied by Matt Dracup, PGM (PADEP), Doug Oberdorf, and Jason Nicholson (EQT). Additional EQT and SPSI representatives on site. Stressed vegetation observed on north-northwest facing slope (fill side) of the Ironman pad on 07/14/2023 by an EQT contractor doing a routine site inspection. EQT representative investigated stressed vegetation on 07/17/2023 and identified it as a brine release and notified the Department. It was further investigated by EQT on 07/17/2023 w/ interim remediation activities starting on 07/18/2023. According to EQT, an approx. 5 ft x 2 ft pool of fluid was observed within area of stressed vegetation and fluid was observed sprinkling out. The overall area of stressed vegetation was approximately 25 ft x 25 ft. The release was estimated over a barrel and Act 2 remediation is anticipated. The source of the leak was identified as a small pinhole in cushion elbow at the northern most corner of the pad from the buried common dump line transferring brine flowback from the GPUs to the ASTs; approx. 70 ft northeast, away from the stressed vegetation area. Operator discovery and pre-remediation conductivity levels and incident writeup requested.Inspection observations: Area of stressed vegetation and pooled production fluid observed on fill slope below northwestern edge of pad and below compressor building on the pad. Among pooled fluid, an oily sheen was also observed. The impacted area appeared to be approx. 25 ft. x 25 ft. The area was covered with a plastic tarp upon arriving on site (Photos 1-7). SPSI crew preparing and beginning excavation to locate source of leak and begin remediation measures. Potholes to be dug on pad around approximate area of leak source to gain extent of fluid. Elevated conductivity observed within impacted area yielded readings of 14.62 mS, 9.96 mS. Readings beyond edge of impacted area, on the more northern edge of the area, displayed a reading of 1.87 mS. Additional readings within vegetation beyond edge of affected area were taken and yielded levels of 1.03 and within the area beyond the fence approximately 5 ft. at the bottom of the slope, 1.98 mS was observed within vegetation. Readings taken within the Unnamed Tributary to Daniels Run, below impacted area approximately 125 ft. north of the impacted area. Readings obtained within water and sediment of the stream w/ levels at 0.43-0.86 mS. Readings obtained within retentive berm along southeastern edge of site below pad; readings taken in water and within sediment yielded 0.33 mS and 0.60 mS (8-16). Readings taken at southern corner of the vegetated swales outlet structure, both in and around; readings of 0.46 mS within water and 0.59 mS within mud around the structure observed (17). SPSI began excavating a pothole, approx. 3 ft in depth; pooled fluid observed within. Conductivity reading within excavated hole was 6.30 mS. Vegetated berm adjacent to hole, above impacted area, displayed a reading of 0.34 mS (18-20). Additional readings within vegetation beyond western edge of impacted area displayed 2.21-6.44 mS (21-23). Reading in fluid contained within secondary containment around ASTs w/ level of 7.20 mS. Due to observed release of production fluid within vegetation on site and potential for fluid to impact WOC downslope of impacted area, violations of 78a.54, SWMA 301, 78a.57(a), and 91.34(a) are being issued. Additional violations of 78a.66(b)(2) for failure to report within 2 hours, 78a.66(b)1(i), 78a.66(b)1(ii), and 91.33(a) for threatening WOC pollution, 5 gallons not completely contained and failure to report to DEP and downstream users are being issued. Additional follow up inspections to be conducted to monitor WOC downslope of impacted area.

Report Details

Unconventional: Yes

Comments: This follow-up inspection was conducted in order to assess overall site conditions after multiple spills occurred on Pad B since fracing began on the pad early in the year. Pad B is now completely empty with the exception of the nine well heads which are not staged for production. Very little stormwater is present on the pad surface. Puddles on the pad surface had an electrical conductivity (EC) between 500 and 600 uS/cm. The EC of the fluid in the sump in the north stormwater channel was 550 uS/cm. The fluid at the channel outlet at the northeast corner of the pad had an EC of 628 uS/cm. The fluid in each of the well cellars has a petroleum sheen on it. On Pad A, six wells are staged for production. Six GPUs are present within secondary containment. The GPUs and containment appear to be in good condition. Violations remain outstanding for the produced water release discovered by the Department on Pad B on 7/11/22.

properties.content:
Report Details

Permit API: 129-25570
Unconventional: Yes
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Hempfield Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 7/15/2026
Comments: On 7/15/2026, the Department conducted an inspection at the Schimizzi S and M 1 well site in Hempfield Township, Westmoreland County. This inspection follows up to IR 4187078, where violations were left outstanding due to no observable Act 9 sign and available Emergency Response plan (ERP) onsite. At the time of this inspection, no formal NOV Response of any kind has been received from the operator regarding violations issued in 3093059 or any subsequent cleanup that may have been conducted. Since the time of IR 3484420, the soil conductivity onsite appeared to be comparable with that of the surrounding soil. Since the time of IR 3978494, no staining or distressed vegetation was observed around the production tanks.On 4/02/2026, Big Dog Energy representative responded via email to IR 4168852 and stated "As the DEP is aware this well was sold to Murphy Production in 2024. However in regards to the spill there was none. I ordered a new sign to put up just so this well can be transferred along with an ERP plan. Should have it within a week to install and get transferred to Murphy" (IR 4174382). However, the well site was unchanged at the time of the following inspection conducted on 4/27/2026 (IR 4187078). The following was observed during the inspection:No Act 9 sign is present at the well site entrance, and no ERP was found anywhere onsite (photo 12). The production tanks appear to be sound at the time of inspection. However, they still lack compliant secondary containment to 78a.64(a), as is required at unconventional well sites (photos 7, 8, 10, and 11). No staining or distressed vegetation was observed on the ground around the gas well (photos 1-3). The well postings onsite include contact information for Dorso LP (photo 6). Outstanding violations issued against the operator's posted information are being overseen by the OG SubSurface team. The additional piping and production equipment that does not appear to be in use remains onsite (photos 4 and 5). A violation was issued in IR 4170358 for failure to remove equipment that is not necessary for production, in accordance with in accordance with OGA3216(C).The well site overall exhibits greater than 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth. No accelerated erosion and sedimentation concerns are observed at this time (photos 1, 9, and 12).Based on observations from this inspection, violations that were continued in IR 4187078 remain outstanding, as it appears that no corrective action has been taken onsite since the date of that inspection and no formal NOV Response of any kind to IR 3093059 has been received to date.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: ARMAC RESOURCES LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 5/31/2023
Violation Code: 78.91(a) - PLUGGING - GENERAL PROVISIONS - Upon abandoning a well, the owner or operator failed to plug the well to stop the vertical flow of fluids or gas within the well bore under 25 Pa. Code §§ 78.92—78.98 or an approved alternate method.
Violation ID: 997557
Permit API: 123-45286
Unconventional: No
County: Warren
Municipality: Warren City
Inspection Type: Compliance Evaluation
Inspection Date: 5/31/2023
Comments: This well was inspected as part of an ongoing gas migration case and to note any changes in the wells characteristics. At the time of inspection the well was shut in and a ounces per square inch gauge was installed on the of the 1-1/2 ports of the production wing. Upon opening the ball valve the gauge read 2 ounces per square inch. The 1-1/2 tubing stub at the top of the well was then open and a MSA Altair 5X calibrated on 05/16/2023 was placed in the well bore and 24% methane by volume was detected. No major changes in pressures of percentages were observed from previous inspections. The operator has not demonstrated that this well has been properly plugged to stop the vertical flow of gas or fluids within the well bore and the violation will will continue. Armac's plugging contractor has been in touch and stated that they plan to be on this well with in a couple of weeks at which time they will discuss their plan in more detail with the department.

Comments: On 8/10/23 at 1201 hrs., I conducted an incident inspection of Madtick Development Corp.'s Musser Associates 2 well site (API 063-32934) in East Mahoning Twp., Indiana Co. The inspection was conducted in response to a phone call received on 8/10/23 from the landowner, indicating that a production fluid release was observed at the well site. The landowner unsuccessfully attempted to contact the operator, and then reported the release to the Department. Upon inspection of the site, stressed/dead vegetation was observed around the production fluid tank onsite, and in an adjacent corn field. The area of dead vegetation appears to be approximately 30-45 feet wide and extends approximately 200-250 feet to the North of the well site. The release appears to be originating from a tank onsite. The tank appears to be empty. The release appears to be over 1 barrel of fluid. In addition to the release, it was observed that the well is equipped for production. A well tag is not affixed to the completed well. A site ID sign is posted, but is illegible and does not display the required information.Violations of 91.33(A), 78.66(a), and 78.66(b) are being cited for failure by the operator to report the release, and are immediately being closed as 'unresolvable'.Violations of OGA 3211(G) and OGA 3211(H) are cited for the lack of site ID sign and well tag. Violations of 78.57(a), SWMA 301, SWMA 302(A), and SWMA 610(1) are cited for the release of production fluids from the tank onto the ground. The violations will be resolved upon remediation of the site and attainment of an Act 2 standard. Please refer to page 3 of this Notice of Violation regarding a written response describing how you intend to remediate the release anddemonstrate attainment of an Act 2 standard.

Comments: Onsite to investigate Complaint # 373782 dated 7/20/2023 and a follow-up inspection to Inspection Report # 3589928 dated 7/21/2023. Onsite with DEP staff Alicia Furey and Lucas Eichner to collect a water sample from the earthen dike. The earthen dike is retaining fluid inside the bottom of the entire dike. There is approximately 4-5" of oily water pooled inside the dike. The dike drain remains closed and plugged. Water flowing into a separator barrel on top of a steel oil tank could be heard from the ground.Prior to the site visit water samples of the Bellows Spring was collected for analysis. There are 4 separate pipes flowing water into the cistern for the spring. Each pipe was identified, labeled, and sampled separately.After collecting samples from the earthen dike, DEP staff walked the hillside between the tank battery and Bellows Spring. The goal was to investigate any other oil and gas activity that may be located above the spring and that would be a potential contributor to the impact of the Bellows Spring. There was nothing observed between the tank battery and the Bellows Spring relating to oil and gas activity.At 2:05pm Mr. Rhoades was called via phone by the Department. The current condition of the tank battery was discussed with Mr. Rhoades and he indicated that a water truck is scheduled for next week to empty the dike and the brine tanks. Mr. Rhoades also stated that he has hired Moody and Associates as a consultant and that a check was in the mail to obtain their services. The Department clearly communicated the importance and urgency of starting the cleanup process at the site including the earthen dike area. Mr. Rhoades seemed to understand and asked if the water was good to drink yet in Reno and if individual households are being tested. I explained to Mr. Rhoades that samples have been taken from the spring by Oil and Gas Operations and that I was unaware of any other sampling/testing. It was also stated that the "Do not Consume" advisory has not yet been lifted from my knowledge at the time. The phone call was concluded with Mr. Rhoades indicating that he is starting the process to clean things up.

Comments: On July 19, 2021, I conducted an inspection of the Lamacz 1 oil and gas well in Penn Township, Westmoreland County. The inspection was conducted in response to a reportable release received on 7/19/2021. On 7/19/2021, the Operator reported that a landowner hit a valve while mowing on Friday July 16, 2021 and did not notify the Operator emergency number. The Operator located the voice mail on 7/19/2021 and responded immediately. I spoke with Marc Jacobs regarding the release. Mr. Jacobs indicated that approximately 40 barrels of fluid was lost from the brine tank. Additionally, Mike Walor Woodard & Curran was contracted to evaluate and remediate the impacted area. Mr. Walor indicated that the impacted material would be remediated in accordance with the Act 2 standards. At the time of inspection, The Operator was removing fluid from the fiberglass brine tank with a vac truck. I observed a significant amount of crude oil and brine spilled to the ground and resulted in a flow path approximately 500’ down gradient from the well through the landowners mowed field. The spill appeared to emanate at or near the brine tank valve. I spoke with the landowner, who admitted to hitting the valve with the mower deck on Friday July 16, 2021. The landowner also indicated that it was raining when the valve was struck. The impacted material was not observed in or appeared to have entered waters of the commonwealth. In addition to the spill, the fiberglass brine tank appeared to have been previously leaking and repaired prior to the release. A vertical dark stripe was visible on the side of the fiberglass below what appeared to be two fiberglass patches applied to the brine tank. The Department is seeking clarification on when the patches were applied and why the patched were needed. I recommend that the Operator design, construct, maintain, and reasonably protect the brine tank from unauthorized acts of third parties. The fluid lost also appears to be crude oil. The Department is seeking clarification in regard to the amount of crude oil contained within the brine tank as the brine tank was not equipped with secondary containment. Violations are being issued based on the observations made during this inspection. Additional violations maybe forthcoming pending further investigation.

Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Date: 2/01/2024
Comments: On February 1, 2024, inspection conducted at the Athena well pad in Washington Township, Westmoreland County. ESCGP approval was obtained on January 10, 2022 and expires on January 9, 2027. Present were Olympus Energy representative Laura Karosic, independent consultants Brad Latimer and Jeff Leary, and myself. Briefly present was Olympus Energy representative Jim Noon. This inspection was conducted in response to a spill that was discovered while removing containment from the pad. The operator reports discovering at least 5 gallons of an oily material on the well pad. The following was observed:At the time of inspection, the Act 9 sign was installed at the entrance of the access road and was not obstructed from view by vegetation, in accordance with 78a.55 (see photo 1). The ERP, PPC plan, ESCGP approval letter, and E and S inspection logs were onsite (see photos 2-4). However, no E and S inspections beyond November 22, 2023 were available in the log onsite. The access road appeared to be stable with no evidence of accelerated erosion or sedimentation. The well pad was excavated at the time of inspection to install flow lines to the newly-drilled Utica wells onsite (see photos 6 and 14). A stained area of approximately 65 feet by 55 feet (according to measurements taken by the operator) was observed on the pad (see photos 7-10). Onsite consultants stated that they attempted to dig into the stained gravel in an attempt to gauge how far down the staining goes, but were unable. Ms. Karosic reported conductivity readings below 1,000 Microsiemens in the stained area. She also reported that the well pad drainages were closed-in upon discovery of the stained area. She informed the DEP that sampling will be conducted and remediation will be handled by Moody and Associates within the coming week, and additional information will be provided as additional discoveries are made in their investigation. The operator anticipates to conduct remediation in accordance with Act 2. Because it is unknown when the secondary containment failed, the DEP inquired on the timeline that it was on the pad. The aforementioned representatives informed the DEP that containment was first placed on the pad in late July of 2023 for drilling of the two Utica wells. Additional containment layers and rig mats were placed approximately six months ago for Completions, and the two Utica wells currently await to be fracked. GPU units onsite are equipped with raised secondary containment skids (see photo 13). Production tanks were placed in secondary containment with no observed leaks with the containment (see photo 11). The six additional wells onsite that appear to be in production were equipped with well tags, and did not appear to have any evidence of leaks or discharge on the ground around them at the time of inspection (see photo 15). All other containments onsite that appeared to contain regulated substances were placed in secondary containment. PCSM BMP's appeared to be constructed according to the plans onsite. The Department checked the downslope well pad drainages for any evidence of staining or impact from the newly discovered spill. No staining, distressed vegetation, or anything that would substantiate the occurrence of a recent spill was observed (see photos 5 and 18-25). Before departing from site, the DEP spoke with Olympus representative Jim Noon to inform him that the onsite E and S inspection log was incomplete, and that this has also been observed at another Olympus Pad. He stated that Olympus will conduct additional follow up with their EI's and provide them electronically for this site.Based on observations from this inspection, violations are being issued for releasing this unknown oily substance to the surface of the well pad. An additional violation is being issued for threatening the WOTC, as the ground water depth appears to be shallow at approximately 15-200 centimeters in this area according to surveys conducted by the USDA.

Unconventional: Yes

Comments: On December 7, 2022, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted a routine site inspection at the Beech Resources ISA Well Psd. This inspection is to follow up after discovering an area of elevated soil conductivity on the west end of the well pad slope on November 29, 2022. Beech Resources was in the process of rigging down after completing stimulation of newly drilled wells. Beech Resources has placed a tarp over the area of elevated soil conductivity discovered on November 29, 2022. Due to recent weather, Beech has not been able to begin the remediation of the impacted soil. The DEP screened the immediate area around the tarp to see if the area of impact expanded. An area to the south of the tarp was discovered to also have elevated soil conductivity ranging from 800 uS/cm to over range readings of the soil conductivity meter. The upper limit range of the soil conductivity meter is 4,000 uS/cm. Don Stevenson with Beech Resources arrived onsite and DEP showed the newly discovered area. The new area is another 30 ft. wide and about 120 ft. long and is adjacent to the area found on November 29, 2022. Mr. Stevenson and DEP observed the containment liner in the area used for the frack rig. A small hole in the liner was observed in the area up gradient of the area of elevated soil conductivity. Mr. Stevenson said that Beech is planning to begin removing the containment onsite today.No new violations noted. Outstanding violations remain from Inspection Report 3464887.

Unconventional: No

Inspection Date: 4/17/2026
Comments: On April 17, 2026, the DEP conducted a FUI of Oil and Gas Mgmt Inc's Armstrong 2 gas well following IR4155454 where violations were continued for an inadequately stabilized shared and direct access road. Present during today's inspection is DEP ET Rosie Wise.A NOV response has yet to be received from the operator of this gas well following IR3891447 when viols were issued however, the DEP has been in communication with the other operator who utilizes the shared portion of the access road. IR4155472 documents the other operator stating they would visit the site to assess the shared road. Observations collected of the shared access road during IR 4155454 include deep erosion rills with water actively flowing down the access road and an exposed and cracked open culvert pipe. During IR 4155454, the DEP requested the operator(s) provide the DEP with a written timeline of remedial actions to repair the access road. To date, this written timeline this has yet to be received. At the time of this inspection, the DEP observed the shared portion of the access road (Wildcat Road) to be graded with all erosion rills and the exposed culvert pipe removed. Dirt that appeared to be removed from the road during grading was observed to be piled up along the right side of the shared access road. Clumps of this dirt was also observed in the floodway/streambank of a stream located directly downslope and to the right of the shared access road. The broken culvert pipe was observed to be lying on the ground adjacent to the access road, another piece of culvert piping that the broken piece was connected to was still observed to be in the ground and partially buried. Water was not observed to be actively discharging out of this culvert outlet as it appears the inlet may be blocked and resulting in seepage of water along other portions of the access road downslope. The DEP notes that no E and S controls appeared to be installed anywhere along the shared access road. Violations are being issued at this time for sediment entering the Waters of the Commonwealth (WOC) and for failure to install E and S controls during earth disturbance activity.At the time of this inspection, no other active E and S issues were observed along the shared portions of Wildcat Road, however, the shared road was not stabilized with gravel and is exhibiting the potential for other E and S issues to occur.The DEP recommends the Operator remove the sediment from the WOC, stabilize the access road, unblock/replace the culvert pipe and install E and S controls along the access road to prevent any further e and s issues.Upon inspection of the direct portion of the access road, conditions appear to be unchanged, the DEP observed large areas of the access road to be flooded. An exposed pipe was observed alongside the access road, however no methane or other odor was detected, the exposed portion of the pipe did not appear to be compromised.At the time of this inspection, the gas well site was still observed to be overgrown with vegetation. A well tag with all required information posted on it was observed to be fixed to a heavily rusted wellhead. No active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from the surface of the gas wellhead or other production equipment on site at this time, however, a strong gas odor and hissing sound was observed to be coming from the lower portion of the gas wellhead. OGI assistance is being requested at this time to assess the gas wellhead for a gas release. Refer to IR 4183514 for the continuation of violations for heavily rusted production equipment.While onsite, the DEP called the number on the well tag in an attempt to notify the operator of the new violations, however, the number was not in service. Based on today's inspection, violations issued for an inadequately stabilized access road are being continued, and new violations are being issued for sediment entering WOC and failure to implement E and S controls.

Comments: This inspection is taking place in response to a spill reported by the operator on 4/7/21 at approximately 11:53 AM. According to the operator, while drilling at the Bakerstown Rd Pad 8H, "a synthetic oil-based drilling mud (SOBM) was inadvertently sent to the gas buster. The SOBM flowed through the flare line, filled the eco tank and then was released from the top of the flare stack. The onsite vac unit and absorbent pads were utilized to collect standing SOBM." The following is observed: The Pioneer 76 rig is on site. Due to the nature of the incident, drilling operations have been temporarily suspended until the flare stack is back in operation. SPSI is on site conducting remediation. Material is being removed from the riprap lined pad ditch line (2, 3, 7, & 8). It appears that impacted water has gotten into the perforated drainpipe and migrated along it (7). The extent of this migration is not known; however, the outlet box is observed to be free of impacted material at this time. The operator has closed the outlet pipe to the level spreader. The Department requests that the operator notify the WQS prior to reopening the drain. In the interim, the EI stated that the outlet box will be monitored and drained using a vac truck as needed. The Department requested photographs of the extent of the excavation necessary to remediate the spill, specifically around the perforated drainpipe. The EI stated that the plan was to excavate until they reached "clean" pipe and cut away the impacted portion. The Department requests that the operator notify the WQS if this course of action needs to be modified. The Department also recommended that the flare stack either be moved away from the ditch line or have secondary containment installed. According to the EI, the site will be remediated under Act 2 requirements. The Department requests a copy of the waste manifest when it is available. The SDS sheet for the drilling mud and PPC/ERP is on-site. According to the secondary containment inspection record at the site, 4/7/21 is listed as the only inspection/incident to have occurred. The Department requests information on when the secondary containment was installed and when the most recent drilling operations began at the site. Based on this inspection, violations are being issued for the spill. Pending the operator’s response, more violations may be issued.

Comments: Site inspection by EPS Justin Abbott. Inspection conducted in response to spill notification submitted by EQT for the COP Tract 551-B pad. Inspection accompanied by EQT Lead EHS Coordinator Mark Barbier. Meeting on site with EQT Company Man Mike Hood. Weather conditions at time of inspection are partly cloudy, humid and 73 degrees F. Well stimulation activity is ceased at this time while EQT reviews SOPs.According to the Standard Detail Report, the spill notification was submitted by Mr. Barbier. At around 0800 hours, US Well Services was swabbing the well to switch over from the 6H to the 7H well. At that time, the open topped blender hopper overflowed releasing an estimated 140 barrels of fluid to containment, of which an unknown quantity of fluid overtopped the containment structures. During discussions on site with Mr. Barbier, the estimation was based on the fact that the pumps may have been releasing 20 barrels per minute for 7 minutes, although the exact volume can not be determined. The Department conducted conductivity screenings using an Oakton PCTS 50 meter and a Hanna Groline Soil Conductivity meter. Pooled fluid remaining within the containment structure was observed with conductivity readings between 7-8 mS/cm. Fluid within the north pad ditch and sumps outside of containment ranged from 3.92-5.37 mS/cm. Visual evidence of spilled fluid extended from a brushy area at the north conrer of the pad, along the entire ditch perimeter into the woods at the eastern corner of the pad where appeared to collect in a row of silt sock. Two vac trucks are present on site. One truck is vacuuming fluid from containment, a second truck is pumping spilled fluid collecting at he low point in the eastern corner of the pad ditch (photo 9). Visual observations near the blender unit indicated that fluid was released with sufficient force to release frac sand from the hopper. Two drums of frac sand were hand shoveled from the spill area (photo 10). Friction reducer material was also observed on pad rock outside containment. On the pad surface, spilled fluid is observed leaking through pad rock under the working tank secondary containment (photo 5). Pad rock affected by spilled fluid under containment is estimated to cover an area of 250 feet in length by 25-40 feet in width. The north ditch line channel is estimated at 400 feet in length with spilled fluid flowing an additional 25-50 feet off the north and east corners of the pad (photos 4 and 8). During discussions with Mr. Hood, when the well switch over occurs, down well fluid volumes are reduced and the blender valves must be adjusted to correspond to the reduced flow rate. Mr Hood indicated that the spill was caused by the blender operator falling asleep and failing to close a valve connecting the blender pumps to the working tanks during the well switch. Prior to site departure, Andy Steffee, Project Manager with Creston Environmental, arrived on site with a crew to begin conducting site characterization and sampling activity. Based on unknown volume of fluid spilled, Mr.Barbier indicated that EQT will immediately begin Act 2 remediation work. Well stimulation activity is expected to last into August at this location. Violations noted during this inspection and outstanding violations are extended.

Well stimulation activity is ceased at this time while EQT reviews SOPs.According to the Standard Detail Report, the spill notification was submitted by Mr. Barbier. At around 0800 hours, US Well Services was swabbing the well to switch over from the 6H to the 7H well. At that time, the open topped blender hopper overflowed releasing an estimated 140 barrels of fluid to containment, of which an unknown quantity of fluid overtopped the containment structures. During discussions on site with Mr. Barbier, the estimation was based on the fact that the pumps may have been releasing 20 barrels per minute for 7 minutes, although the exact volume can not be determined. The Department conducted conductivity screenings using an Oakton PCTS 50 meter and a Hanna Groline Soil Conductivity meter. Pooled fluid remaining within the containment structure was observed with conductivity readings between 7-8 mS/cm. Fluid within the north pad ditch and sumps outside of containment ranged from 3.92-5.37 mS/cm. Visual evidence of spilled fluid extended from a brushy area at the north conrer of the pad, along the entire ditch perimeter into the woods at the eastern corner of the pad where appeared to collect in a row of silt sock. Two vac trucks are present on site. One truck is vacuuming fluid from containment, a second truck is pumping spilled fluid collecting at he low point in the eastern corner of the pad ditch (photo 9). Visual observations near the blender unit indicated that fluid was released with sufficient force to release frac sand from the hopper. Two drums of frac sand were hand shoveled from the spill area (photo 10). Friction reducer material was also observed on pad rock outside containment. On the pad surface, spilled fluid is observed leaking through pad rock under the working tank secondary containment (photo 5). Pad rock affected by spilled fluid under containment is estimated to cover an area of 250 feet in length by 25-40 feet in width. The north ditch line channel is estimated at 400 feet in length with spilled fluid flowing an additional 25-50 feet off the north and east corners of the pad (photos 4 and 8). During discussions with Mr. Hood, when the well switch over occurs, down well fluid volumes are reduced and the blender valves must be adjusted to correspond to the reduced flow rate. Mr Hood indicated that the spill was caused by the blender operator falling asleep and failing to close a valve connecting the blender pumps to the working tanks during the well switch. Prior to site departure, Andy Steffee, Project Manager with Creston Environmental, arrived on site with a crew to begin conducting site characterization and sampling activity. Based on unknown volume of fluid spilled, Mr.Barbier indicated that EQT will immediately begin Act 2 remediation work. Well stimulation activity is expected to last into August at this location. Violations noted during this inspection and outstanding violations are extended.
